reviews.text: How human beings connect, and how they can become isolated based on a variety of factors, is the key question at the heart of The Social Network. As time changes, and technology continues to evolve, these universal questions will continue to live on.
reviews.author: Joshua Stevens

reviews.text: David Fincher’s The Social Network explores a side of college life not usually seen in movies, and scrutinizes the ones that usually are.
reviews.author: Atreyo Palit

reviews.text: There's so much story in this and provided a great platform for Jesse Eisenberg. It definitely feels like a lot of liberties with this true story but that doesn't make it less entertaining.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: This is a "Top Ten" film for me. The performances, direction, cinematography, score, and of course, the incredible Aaron Sorkin screenplay make this film a classic.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: The Social Network has the potential to be a classic, a masterpiece for our times that captures early 21st century life, while still offering robust, mature entertainment.
reviews.author: Michael Leader

reviews.text: A film by Fincher that, with a brilliant aesthetic, functions as the voice of expression of a generation silenced by the social isolation behind computers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: There are plenty of pop psychology motivations seeded through the film... but they explain the protagonist about as much as Rosebud does in 'Citizen Kane.' This is a story of hubris and ambition, of friendship and jealousy, of class and cultural cache...
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: [David Fincher and writer Aaron Sorkin] elevate what could have been popular fodder into a serious, entertaining, and engaging drama that, through its depth and insight, regards business and social existence in the digital age with a critical eye.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Social Network will go down as one of the best movies of the 21st century, and potentially one of the best movies of all time. It’s Sorkin, Fincher, Eisenberg, and Garfield all at the top of their game.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: The Social Network is another masterful piece of cinema, this time delivered by not one but two magnificent filmmakers. David Fincher and Aaron Sorkin employ their mutual perfectionism and meticulousness to create an extraordinarily engaging narrative.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Equally absorbing are its themes of friendship and loyalty in a playground of petty politics. A superb Jesse Eisenberg as the insensitive, conflicted genius was a revelatory match for Fincher's technical talent.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: The Social Network is an electrifying look into Frankenstein's laboratory.   [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Jordan

reviews.text: The craft on display is impeccable like every Fincher production, and there’s an equally brilliant screenplay to support him.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: A perfectly poignant and cautionary tale about how the biggest influencers in tech began and continue to operate today.
reviews.author: Nathan Mattise

reviews.text: An emotional and suspenseful story...a moral tale about the sweet smell of success.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: Much, much better than a film about Facebook has any right to be...
reviews.author: James McMahon

reviews.text: The Social Network posits that perhaps the tastiest cinematic treat is one that renders its audience gleefully captivated until they transcend into a fugue dream state.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: Who knew coding and depositions could be exciting? Fincher's direction is surgical, Sorkin's script is a thing of beauty and the young cast is superb. The Social Network is outstanding. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The combination of rapid fire dialogue, driven performances, and impeccable editing give The Social Network an incredible sense of energy.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: A decade later, it plays more like a supervillain origin story. It's There Will Be Blood if Daniel Plainview was a dweeby computer programmer who drank lots of Mountain Dew.
reviews.author: Sean Price

reviews.text: Decent intrigue, rivalrous backstabbing, and a little courtroom-style contention.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The best of Aaron Sorkin's razor-sharp writing and David Fincher's visual style come together to bring to life the riveting true story...
reviews.author: Film Companion Staff

reviews.text: It's a gripping adaptation of Ben Mezrich's book, which paints Zuckerberg as both arrogant opportunist and naive underdog.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: An extraordinarily good film featuring a more disciplined Fincher, a more visual Sorkin, and a cast that works together to bring it all to vibrant and disturbing life.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Although the film has some very good qualities ... it didn't present the characters as any more than money hungry entrepreneurs ready to back stab anyone that stands in their way.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: There are so many interesting nuggets in the film.
reviews.author: Nikhat Kazmi

reviews.text: The Social Network unfolds with the wildfire energy of any good idea that grows into a great one.
reviews.author: Felicia Feaster

reviews.text: The Social Network is a very smart film about very smart people, and more importantly, the relationships of those people.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: The Social Network isn't only a great film but it's a classic for a new era in filmmaking.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: he pairing with Sorkin has helped Fincher create his best film to date.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: It's exhilarating to see a movie with this much verbal complexity succeed at being so entertaining.
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: Sorkin's intoxicating, rapid-fire dialogue couple[s} with Fincher's striking imagery to create a wholly immersive viewing experience.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Sorkin's dialogue is captivating, full of humanity and humor. Fortunately, the cast is at the same level as the excellent screenplay.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: A rare example of what can happen when a director, writer, cast, composer, and subject matter all work together perfectly.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Quite possibly (if not definitively) the best mainstream movie of the decade.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: The Social Network is about the establishment of one very popular site, but because of the way it is done, the film is as personal as movies get.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: For all intents and purposes of the film, Eisenberg is on the mark.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: David Fincher's internet epic is an incisively written and impressively controlled biopic where captivating legal drama meets new-media ambition. Jesse Eisenberg exudes a scary confidence and insensitivity in this relentless character study.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: A tight and intriguing two hours of cinema, which despite its subject matter, manages to remain entertaining and thought provoking throughout.
reviews.author: Lee Cassanell

reviews.text: In its cold, almost forensic way, this is as tense and exciting as it is absorbing. It's a miracle, really.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Screenwriter Aaron Sorkin turns the site's formative years into a morality tale for our times.
reviews.author: Dónal Lynch

reviews.text: In keeping with the spirit of the age, Zuckerberg's fantasy isn't toppling the system; it's being successful within it.
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: Fincher is at pains to show that everyone involved in the legal talks believed they were in the right. That he does so successfully is what makes the action so riveting.
reviews.author: Kaleem Aftab

reviews.text: Watching The Social Network was so epic it was like watching the Superbowl, except it was a Superbowl in reverse.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: It is director David Fincher's equivalent of Orson Welles' Citizen Kane: the story of a capitalist who is awe-inspiring in some ways, but tragic in others; enviably clever and driven, but also repellently ruthless and treacherous.
reviews.author: Christopher Tookey

reviews.text: An immaculate realization of clichés, a multi-billion-dollar lawsuit transmuted into a low-stakes male weepie, a bunch of college-movie stereotypes at play in a world of cruelly precise images...
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: Even in a year flooded with excellent dramas, The Social Network is a standout.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The Social Network, just like its subject, is the pop culture phenomenon of the new generation.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: It's true that The Social Network is splendid in its own right. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: In The Social Network Generation Facebook gets a movie almost worthy of them, and this fact, being so unexpected, makes the film feel more delightful than it probably, objectively, is.
reviews.author: Zadie Smith

reviews.text: The performances of Eisenberg as Mark Zuckerberg and Justin Timberlake as the Napster shyster Sean Parker are award-worthy. Andrew Garfield as Ernest Saverin, also gives an impressive performance.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Fincher does, at least, make decent entertainment out of such inherently unprepossessing subjects as computer use and legal hearings.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: A zesty advertisement for the further meaningless Facebookization of our daily routines, and the further squandering of our free time.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: The film keeps teasing at bigger themes when it's really drivel.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: What a terrific movie!
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: A giddy, two-hour rush of hot-blooded vertiginous dialogue and cucumber-cool cinematic curlicues.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It captures the essence of selfishness and treachery, all under the guise of creating a system geared toward making it easier for college kids to get laid. And sure enough, in the end, just about everybody gets screwed.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: The Social Network is a spellbinding and compelling story with top notch performances and flawless directing.
reviews.author: Matt Joseph

reviews.text: Fincher keeps the movie's tech-y elements on the periphery, focusing instead on the time-honored dramatic elements of isolation, determination, avarice and betrayal.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: The Social Network is splendid entertainment from a master storyteller, packed with energetic incident and surprising performances.
reviews.author: Scott Foundas

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's amazing script and several great performances make this one of the best movies of 2010.
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: The Social Network may not turn out to be the definitive movie made about the plugged-in generation, but it's a pretty good start.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: Fincher's keen eye for direction and Sorkin's sharp script make this worth seeing for fans and non-fans of [Facebook] alike.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Director David Fincher seems drawn to these stories of misguided rebels who become monsters in their attempts to reorder the world.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Even if you've never touched a computer in your life, you'll find plenty to be fascinated by in this movie, as it shows that, whilst technology may be moving fast, the human capacity for hubris will always remain the same.
reviews.author: Laurence Boyce

reviews.text: ... A classic American story of capitalism and greed, friendship and betrayal, fueled by envy and lost innocence ...
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: At last, a movie you can actually discuss afterward. And not just on Facebook or Twitter. No, you'll want to chew it over in person, with friends, for hours.
reviews.author: Leah Rozen

reviews.text: It's hard work making a character you don't like into a character you don't like, but can still respect.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Perhaps we've become a world of Mark Zuckerbergs and it's clear that these filmmakers don't like it one bit.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: It's part Citizen Kane, part Goodfellas, part Revenge of the Nerds and the most entertaining film you never knew you would want to see.
reviews.author: Dave White

reviews.text: The Social Network is so engrossing you don't even notice how heavy handed the films central dramatic irony could be -- that the greatest tool for communication in the modern age was created by someone who has no idea how to relate to other people.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: I've read a lot about The Social Network at this point, mostly raves about how it supposedly captures The Way We Live Now, but no one has really zeroed in on how deliberately alienating it is.
reviews.author: Dan Callahan

reviews.text: You wouldn't think that [Fincher & Sorkin's] talents would gel, yet their collaboration on The Social Network is brilliant ... a gripping tale of ambition and envy, betrayal and resentment.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: That the project is not only a success but one of 2010′s best films is a testament to Fincher's talent as a director and his seemingly perennial ability to surround himself with incredibly astute, like-minded collaborators.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Almost certainly deliberately indebted to [Citizen] Kane, a quality that wordlessly speaks to Zuckerberg's own inflated ego.
reviews.author: Rob Humanick

reviews.text: he Social Network occupies a gray area, in which everybody's perspective is in question, and most of the main characters slip into self-serving, subjective realities. ... an ingenious way to tackle a very curious, contemporary case
reviews.author: Matt Kelemen

reviews.text: There's a real mischievousness to David Fincher's approach.
reviews.author: Bryant Frazer

reviews.text: Enormously entertaining, thought-provoking and fascinating despite a flawed, possibly biased screenplay.
reviews.author: R.L. Shaffer

reviews.text: The merits of Facebook can be debated; the merits of The Social Network are undeniable.
reviews.author: Jordan Hiller

reviews.text: An intellectual property battle ripped from today's headlines that feels like a cyber-thriller, yet it never once turns into a heavy-handed message movie.
reviews.author: Bruce Bennett

reviews.text: An invigorating and vital film.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: The genesis of Facebook as weepy bromance
reviews.author: Fernando F. Croce

reviews.text: full review at Movies for the Masses
reviews.author: Joseph Proimakis

reviews.text: A relevant exploration in to the changing of communication and socializing through a man who built an empire around the inability to tell people how he really felt...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Snappy script, sharp editing, eerily perfect soundtrack and nuanced performances. One of the first films to articulate the psychological power and draw of the internet: what it feeds us and why we feed on it
reviews.author: Marc Fennell

reviews.text: Just how much of the story is really true is anyone's guess but the brilliant script and Eisenberg's performance make it worth seeing in any case.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: The great irony is that the biggest player in the social networking boom proved to be someone so socially retarded he borders on sociopathic at times.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: I'm really not making this up. My best friend Emily called me half an hour before I left to see 'The Social Network.' And guess what she wanted to know? 'This woman who went to high school with us wants to friend me,' she said. 'Do you remember her?'
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Fincher and Sorkin, who clearly acknowledged that the meat of the plot was in examining the diverse characters involved, are to be applauded.
reviews.author: Richard Kattan

reviews.text: The Social Network's portrait of Zuckerberg, replete with the jerky rhythms and constant scanning of the truly net addicted, epitomises that change. For that, and some very fine drama indeed, this film is a must-see.
reviews.author: Julie Rigg

reviews.text: It's a credit to the combined efforts of Fincher and Sorkin that the dramatic tension can (more than once) culminate in the refreshing of a website.
reviews.author: Fiona Williams

reviews.text: This is a beautifully made film by David Fincher with a superb screenplay by Aaron Sorkin.
reviews.author: Margaret Pomeranz

reviews.text: Like Zuckerberg, Fincher excels at data management, delivering vast amounts of information with the utmost clarity and speed.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: This masterful, contentious and gripping biopic downloads us deep inside the control-alt-delete mind of the creator of Facebook, and then throws away the escape key.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Wherever the truth lies, The Social Network is an innately compelling, beautifully crafted insight into the emergence of a global phenomenon and the disintegration of a rare friendship.
reviews.author: Jim Mitchell

reviews.text: A film of our times that captures the spirit of a generation that isn't prepared to wait their turn or pay their dues and instead will make the opportunities for themselves or tear it away from the less ambitious.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: This picture helps convey the significance of the social media revolution; the one that simultaneously brings us together and tears us apart. The Social Network is scarily good. It gets us.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: In a superlative example of art-imitating-life, there was definite alchemy at work on the set of The Social Network...nothing short of a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Alice Tynan

reviews.text: It's a shamelessly biased account, as well as a seductively plausible one, although you have to keep your wits about you to get the full effect.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Fincher has delivered his best work since Seven. An even better period drama than Zodiac and even more relevant to our generation today than Fight Club.
reviews.author: Scott Henderson

reviews.text: Clever, cutting and debateable, The Social Network should inspire discussion -- most likely played out on Facebook -- for months to come.
reviews.author: Julian Shaw

reviews.text: It doesn't take but a few minutes into the film for us to realize we're not only watching Fincher's strongest film to date, but the year's as well.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Fincher has constructed a wonderfully balanced tale of a young narcissistic genius in want of status and recognition.
reviews.author: Patrick Kolan

reviews.text: There's a lot to like, yet The Social Network lacks a strong emotional core that is integral to making a good drama truly great.
reviews.author: Anders Wotzke

reviews.text: Not quite a biopic (inventor Zuckerberg is but 26 years old) and not quite a character study, the movie is best thought of as the portrait of an asshole as a young man.
reviews.author: Jeff Meyers

reviews.text: Ultimately it transcends the online world. This is an age-old story of an ambitious person who is able to accomplish much, but loses sight of what's really important.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: A drama of Shakespearean proportions, with the key protagonists all flawed and found wanting
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: It's a bit like getting the scoop and the dirt behind the story, as we watch history unfold before our eyes. Filled with megabits of tension, the story flies at a rapid pace
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: El hábil guión de Aaron Sorkin y la dinámica dirección de David Fincher logran un relato entretenido, que ofrece una visión ambigua - aunque piadosa - del creador de Facebook.
reviews.author: Enrique Buchichio

reviews.text: A riveting, era-defining picture that is guaranteed to make you feel very stupid in comparison and very, very poor.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: An exhilarating, absorbing, fast-moving drama detailing the ugly, angry clash of the old world with the new.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: ...an incredibly solid drama that has plenty to offer both computer buffs and neophytes alike.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: In his first venture over to the dark side, the central performance by Jesse Eisenberg is a revelation. It's Oscar-worthy stuff.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: An anti-charismatic Charles Foster Kane with social issues, class status anger, and homoerotic panic.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: It gets no better than this.
reviews.author: David Edwards

reviews.text: The Social Network is technically flawless, powered by Fincher's dazzling direction...
reviews.author: Catherine Jones

reviews.text: David Fincher's fast-paced business drama adopts the set-up of his 1999 film Fight Club and inverts it.
reviews.author: Anthony Quinn

reviews.text: It's still a little early to start making Oscar noise, but I can see "The Social Network" nabbing several come early next year, including nods for Eisenberg and Timberlake.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Despite the fun of the parties, the intrigue of the legal wranglings and the humour of the dialogue, Fincher and Sorkin never let us forget that we're complicit in their story (or at least 500 million of us are).
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: Business hasn't been this exciting since Gordon Gekko's first outing.
reviews.author: Jonathan Williams

reviews.text: It's riveting stuff...
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: It's Eisenberg's performance that captivates -- icky and icy but strangely sympathetic.
reviews.author: Andy Lowe

reviews.text: Despite all of the betrayal, court cases and double crossing, let's be honest, no-one really cares about the founding of Facebook, but in the hands of David Fincher, however, The Social Network is something of a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Sam Bathe

reviews.text: While it does not really live up to the hyperbolic reviews, this is still a fascinating look at the craft of computer programming and the ostensibly boring question of intellectual property. Of course, it helps that the script is more fiction than fact.
reviews.author: Louis Proyect

reviews.text: El botón de "Me gusta" ha sido presionado. Muchas veces, y con fuerza.
reviews.author: Alex Ramirez

reviews.text: The story of Facebook is given a dramatic twist by the combination of Sorkin's brainy script and Fincher's brawny direction. What emerges is the tale of a computer nerd who only understands relationships if they're online.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: A rich, understated character drama that gleefully exposes the petty playground politics at the centre of one of the internet-era's most bitter court cases.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: A rare and vital film that nails the concerns of privileged post-adolescence in the first few years of the 21st century, and, more universally, draws out eternal themes of truth, subjectivity and envy with an effortless elegance.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: A timeless story of friendship and betrayal which illustrates how our appetite for more can become insatiable, regardless of the consequences.
reviews.author: Graham Young

reviews.text: Fincher melds The Social Network into a riveting study on the perils of power and money, flipping Zuckerberg from socially-maladjusted college student into a young man governed by obsession, greed and entitlement.
reviews.author: Simon Reynolds

reviews.text: The film is almost nothing but scenes of people sitting over glowing screens, or in lawyers' offices, or in bars/diners/clubs. Yet it never seems sedentary. The jabber is intensive.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Like. Poke. Share.
reviews.author: Elliott Noble

reviews.text: Polish up the Oscar and get ready to give it to Eisenberg, an actor whom most people have never seen before.
reviews.author: Steve Rhodes

reviews.text: Put it in a double bill with Zodiac and I might just cry myself to sleep with amazing.
reviews.author: Charlie Lyne

reviews.text: Brilliantly directed, superbly written and impeccably acted, this is a hugely enjoyable, era-defining drama that's gripping, laugh-out-loud funny and ultimately moving -- it's also one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: The film is...kind of like a portrait of Now.
reviews.author: Widgett Walls

reviews.text: Tells an impressive story in an accomplished way about genius and intellect, the corrupting power of greed and pride, and about paying for poor behavior, intentional or otherwise.
reviews.author: Jules Brenner

reviews.text: The Social Network s'impose déjà comme une oeuvre majeure d'une décennie qui ne fait pourtant que commencer.
reviews.author: Jean-François Vandeuren

reviews.text: You can pencil Aaron Sorkin in for the Best Adapted Screenplay Oscar right now.
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: Facebook Founder an Enigma in The Social Network
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Jesse Eisenberg's Zuckerberg is a beautiful, fully textured child of the internet age.
reviews.author: Michael W. Phillips, Jr.

reviews.text: The Social Network is one of the movies for which 2010 will be remembered.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: You’ll be watching in awe as Fincher weaves the scenes of this film together. There’s never a dull moment.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Fincher and Sorkin Have Created a Film Whose Truth is as Subject as it's Presented on Facebook Itself. A Dark, Entertaining Parable.
reviews.author: Jimmy O

reviews.text: A sympathetic examination of how this prickly character [Zuckerberg], and his desperate need for connection, led to an invention that allows millions to connect with each other.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: We have Facebook because some dude got dumped. I can believe that.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: A dizzyingly smart, confident, often riveting drama about the creation of the groundbreaking Web site.
reviews.author: Jon Frosch

reviews.text: Interesting, if unexceptional, but there are bothersome portrayals in the film that just don't ring true. It turns out the there is a good reason for this: these depictions are false. That is a problem.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Watching a movie with a snappy pace, whip-smart dialogue, and so many interesting things to say about where we are as a country right now is such a pleasure.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: "The Social Network" has an unusually difficult task to pull off--it has to make computer programming exciting--and it does so with aplomb.
reviews.author: Christopher Smith

reviews.text: Manipulation is the heart of this film, both in the story being told, and by the filmmakers who molded the true story to fit their agenda.
reviews.author: Lori Hoffman

reviews.text: a virtuoso modern parable about greed, innovation, and betrayal, as well as a compelling portrait of how technology is changing the landscape of both business enterprise and interpersonal relationships
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Here’s a status update: Yes, controlling personalities with Napoleon complexes thrive on the Internet. Too bad this film seems to have been made by as well as about them.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: The Social Network is a sweeping look at the mind, our generation and era, and our future.
reviews.author: Gabe Leibowitz

reviews.text: A glib little morality tale dressed up in trendy togs, and it is to profundity what Facebook is to actual human interaction. But it’s undeniably appealing.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: The film's real achievement stretches beyond the story. When we've all forgotten Facebook, The Social Network will remind us what it was to be part of the generation of Millenials.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Expresses that the most successful personalities are driven by a psychotic need to win.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Chen

reviews.text: A business procedural played with the intensity of a thriller and the ingenuity of a screwball comedy.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: The underlying message in the films seems to be that if these guys just got laid more often we would never have had innovations like Napster and Facebook.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: A great director can take a great script and make a great movie out of any subject matter - such as the creation of Facebook
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The scariest screen villain in a half century, since Psycho's Norman Bates, given that this inscrutable creep actually exists in real life.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Eisenberg gives a performance so captivating that I could sit through the movie again, just to watch him.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: 'Citizen Kane' for the impatient digital era, with that masterpiece's decades-spanning morality tale of loss, hubris, loneliness and revenge compressed into a few years, and with an ex-girlfriend named Erica instead of a sled named Rosebud...
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: The film played well for me while it was playing -- I wasn't bored. But it's far from the best movie I've seen this year.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The movie's lustrous, deep-focus frames and headlong pace are difficult to resist. Its an entertainingly cynical small movie.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Cool, fast, smart and sleek. It's also a surprisingly deep and almost painful reminder of the importance of a real social network - as opposed to, say, Facebook.
reviews.author: Gina Carbone

reviews.text: Bookmark this one on your must-see list.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: The Facebook flick is a kick-in-the-head tale of ambition, friendship and betrayal. Fincher and Sorkin turn hacking, blogging and coding into action scenes.
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: I know I could tell you to 'accept' or 'like' or 'friend' this movie. Instead, I'm just going to tell you to go see it.
reviews.author: Jeff Bayer

reviews.text: Fast-moving, engaging, and even exciting.
reviews.author: Boo Allen

reviews.text: Even if you've never logged on to Facebook, you can still get caught up in the way The Social Network looks at issues of friendship, rivalry, inspiration, and the cutthroat nature of business.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A modern morality tale full of rich performances by a great young cast playing from a smart, canny script. The Social Network is one of the coolest, sharpest films of the year.
reviews.author: Diva Velez

reviews.text: Makes a seemingly dry civil law suit story a fascinating sexy watch.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Like the screwball comedies and film noir staples of yore, The Social Network exhibits an extraordinary gift for gab.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Young adults in today's Entitlement Generation may come away from the film thinking that it's perfectly justifiable to be an a**hole and a misogynist, as long as you get into Harvard and come out a billionaire.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: [Network's rise and fall] relates to the classic gangster film narrative ... More directly, [the film] positions itself as a new Citizen Kane, with its protagonist reaching the heights of a communication empire.
reviews.author: Matthew Sorrento

reviews.text: The Social Network boasts enough great dialogue to fuel a half dozen Oscar-bait movies.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: What happens when a director and writer hate their subject? A well made, but one dimensional hit piece.
reviews.author: Michelle Alexandria

reviews.text: Never before have coding and algorithms been so titillating.
reviews.author: Tim Basham

reviews.text: It is a great many things: a giddy comedy... a marvelous piece of top-shelf cinematic craftsmanship, a consideration of how communication works in a plugged-in world.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The movie may serve to bridge the huge Grand Canyon-like chasm between baby boomers on one side and Gen X and Y'ers on the other, stimulating meaningful discussions about values, viewpoints and ideas.
reviews.author: Keith Cohen

reviews.text: Give it a shot. Unlike Facebook itself, The Social Network has no real flaws.
reviews.author: Karina Montgomery

reviews.text: As great as the film is, you can't overlook the fact that if you knew these people in real life you would block them on Facebook.
reviews.author: Jim Vejvoda

reviews.text: The Social Network is one of the saddest movies ever made
reviews.author: D.K. Holm

reviews.text: [Fincher]crafts a document that analyzes who we are now and where we're at in a way no other motion picture up to now has, and for that reason alone that probable makes the film a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: ...A fascinating, absorbing film well worth friending.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: a self-important, narcissistic glorification of its own significance
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The chill that seeps through The Social Network... is a feature, not a bug: Zuckerberg's is a cold world, and Eisenberg's calculated detachment makes for an astonishingly sophisticated performance...
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: The cinematic union of Sorkin and Fincher for this their first collaboration is brilliant.
reviews.author: Paula Farmer

reviews.text: The story of a groundswell,of an unlikely collaboration between a product and its customers that upended not just the value propositions of Harvard, but of the pre-web economy
reviews.author: Steven Snyder

reviews.text: ... it's flashy as hell given its subject matter. It also doesn't hurt that it's pretty good.
reviews.author: George Wu

reviews.text: ... it's Eisenberg's performance that helps make Zuckerberg the most fascinating and complicated movie character since Daniel Day-Lewis' Daniel Plainview.
reviews.author: Adam Tobias

reviews.text: Fincher is back to the sort of engrossing, immersive storytelling of his best work in Zodiac.
reviews.author: Ian Buckwalter

reviews.text: Nonetheless, having made the occupants of the White House seem believably human in The American President and in The West Wing, Sorkin knows it's better to focus on his characters' hearts, no matter how black, than their coding fingers
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: There's a lot to "Like" about The Social Network.
reviews.author: Tyler Hanley

reviews.text: That is, the possible "openness" of Facebook here hinges on the definitive closed system embodied by this fictional Mark Zuckerberg.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: In the end, The Social Network is not so much about Facebook as it is about the complicated and tortuous social warfare that led to its birth.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: You will know The Social Network is something very special from its first scene.
reviews.author: Charlie McCollum

reviews.text: The Social Network shares creative DNA with a handful of classic, zeitgeist-savvy films like Network and All the President's Men, as well as more recent fare such as The Insider and Michael Clayton.
reviews.author: Lisa Kennedy

reviews.text: The brilliance of Eisenberg's performance is that even when you want to slap his Zuckerberg silly you can't help but admire his creativity, his ambition and his almost religious dedication to the Internet's potential.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: This is the 2010 Oscar season's first drama to live up to the hype and expectations associated with it.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: There's a cool precision and honesty to The Social Network, the story of the founding of Facebook, which guarantees its entertainment value even as it limits its emotional impact.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: It has the staccato wit of a drawing-room comedy, the fatal flaw of a tragic romance and the buzzy immediacy of a front-page headline, all powered by a kinetic engine typically found in an action flick.
reviews.author: Rick Groen

reviews.text: [P]roof that Fincher's directorial verve can imbue virtually any tale with urgency, be it the search for a killer or the search for a killer app.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: Despite the whiz-bang topicality, the headlong intelligence, and the many sharp collegiate scenes, this new-style movie hews pretty closely to an old-style playbook.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: David Fincher and screenwriter Aaron Sorkin have put together a well-acted, intelligent, and compelling film that merits accolades as one of the best films of 2010.
reviews.author: Wilson Morales

reviews.text: The Social Network is a bland title for such a thrilling, ballsy, intelligent movie.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Hallelujah! Finally, a movie with the kind of dialogue we deserve!
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Much of the preliminary discussions about logarithms and formulas are merely geek-speak for most moviegoers, but because Fincher has weaved it all together in a hugely entertaining package, we don't care.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Multifaceted and Brilliant
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: Eisenberg gives us a speeded-up rendition of his previous performances, but it fits. There's also fine cinematography by Jeff Cronenweth and softly pulsating music by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: What a joy to sit in a theater and be engaged, surprised, challenged, amused.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Fantastic performances, compelling story for teens and up.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: A perfect package to document a bright young thing's meteoric rise and near-fall.
reviews.author: Tricia Olszewski

reviews.text: The Social Network is more a meditation on right vs. wrong than a chronicle of the birth of Facebook and it is a more affecting film because of that.
reviews.author: Daniel Hubschman

reviews.text: An utterly fascinating and compelling work that combines classical dramatic storytelling, a cutting-edge visual style and a steely intelligence equal to that displayed by any of its hyper-brainy characters
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: ...a fabulous post-modern fable.
reviews.author: Bill Gibron

reviews.text: David Fincher's smartly written, expertly told chronicling of the dawn of the Facebook era ... is just that compelling, that engrossing, that hard to resist. Kind of like a certain website I know.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: The best movie ever made about e-commerce, as well as the Internet itself.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: A tale of a social outcast turning the tables, or, if you can't join 'em, beat 'em. This is a valuable, flinty work of reflective zeitgeist, holding up a myriad of mirrors to our own wildly self-promotional selves.
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: Every aspect of the film, from Fincher's beautiful direction to Reznor's emotionally devastating score to each and every performance is absolutely stunning.
reviews.author: Kevin McCarthy

reviews.text: None of these ideas is revolutionary, but The Social Network embeds them in a taut, intellectually exhilarating narrative in which daredevil dialogue simultaneously defines characters and obscures motivations.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: One of the best of 2010. (Parental Review also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: ...an exciting parable about new millennium high tech, money and power.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Sorkin has stripped down the Facebook experience and presents the overlying and often unspoken commitment to its usage. How do others view us?
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Somehow the results come together like the perfect status update.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: If you want to see an enthralling movie about business in the 21st century, forget about that stinker Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: Everyone in The Social Network is smart. Everyone in The Social Network is sarcastic. And that is big fun to watch.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: David Fincher-who managed to make information-overload so gripping in Zodiac-is the ideal director for this story: He sweeps you up into its unexpectedly vibrant world.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: What looks on paper like a static series of dead-end conversations comes to life as a vital, engaging, even urgent parable for our age.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Everyone involved went out and made the film they were trying to make, and it's often funny and generally captivating.
reviews.author: Laremy Legel

reviews.text: You wouldn't think a movie about the creation of a website could be so enthralling, insightful, funny, and complex, but here we are.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: The best aspect of the movie is just how delightfully trashy it is. There are more "oh no he di-in't" moments than in an episode of Jersey Shore.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: The Social Network" is sharp, incisive, insightful and witty. It also touches upon our need -- some may say our addiction -- for human contact, even if it is through a computer.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Lackluster, pedestrian, emotionally hollow and underwhelming despite exquisite cinematography and a timely, initially intriguing premise.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: The Social Network sets out to show you the genesis of a modern Rockefeller, Carnegie or Vanderbilt. In the 21st century, information is the new oil, the new steel. What hasn't changed is the mentality of the tycoon.
reviews.author: Brandon Fibbs

reviews.text: Fincher's approach to the socially significant creation that validated the lonely lives of a nation is to shoot it like he made Fight Club, a surreal dream of financial waste and delusion covered in a deep green and brown color scheme.
reviews.author: Adam Lippe

reviews.text: Eisenberg is superb, playing not the real Mark Zuckerberg but the character created by Sorkin, hyper-alert and obtuse, his voice both taut and tremulous.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: All of these misshapen odds and ends click together for one of the year's most satisfying films so far.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Aiming for greatness and not quite making it, The Social Network will have to settle for solidly consistent. Most major studio releases should be so lucky.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: You may not want to live inside Mark Zuckerberg's head, you may not care for Facebook, but you'll be drawn into the world of the film utterly. It's a massive achievement.
reviews.author: Shawn Levy

reviews.text: Densely written and expertly directed with performances that rank among the year's best...
reviews.author: Justin Strout

reviews.text: Even with his constantly affectless expression, Eisenberg gives Zuckerberg just enough vulnerability to make you not entirely hate him.
reviews.author: Alison Gang

reviews.text: The writing is strong, and the drama -- the drama of betrayal -- is ever present.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The Social Network is a film for now, even if in the realm of computer time 2003 seems like a lifetime ago. It's riveting entertainment, and a must-see.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: A fly-on-the-wall objective look at a personality who is at once public and unknowable, in metaphor for current instantaneous non-face-to-face madness.
reviews.author: Donald J. Levit

reviews.text: This account of Facebook's founder, and of the website's explosive growth, quickly lifts you to a state of exhilaration, and pretty much keeps you there for two hours.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Relies mainly on great dialogue and strong performances from its young cast to propel a story so riveting that it transcends the film's ugly reputation as The Facebook Movie.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: It's ironic that only a week after Oliver Stone's Wall Street sequel came out, The Social Network schools the old man by absolutely nailing the new generation of rich jerkwads
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: It's Fight Club without Marla.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Weeks after seeing it, moments from it will haunt you.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: It's a smart bomb of a film that illustrates how technology and innovation influence human behavior.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: One of the many remarkable things about David Fincher's movie The Social Network is the constant realization, as you watch, that this movie should by all rights have been exceedingly dull.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: In the opening few minutes of The Social Network, all you see are two college kids yakking, and it's the most enthralling movie sequence of the year.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: It's astonishing that a movie mostly set in front of computer screens and in deposition rooms, a movie where the end is already known, has the hold of a suspense film.
reviews.author: Carrie Rickey

reviews.text: The Social Network is terrific entertainment - an unlikely thriller that makes business ethics, class distinctions and intellectual-property arguments sexy
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: In some ways Fincher, who has portrayed serial killers both fictional ('Seven') and real ('Zodiac'), has never presented a character as remorselessly vicious as the implacable cyberpunk.
reviews.author: Rossiter Drake

reviews.text: Fincher has made quite a few terrific films, from Se7en to the underrated Zodiac. But this time he's outdone himself. The Social Network is riveting from start to finish, and a master class in directing.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: The Social Network sometimes relegates the actual effects of Facebook to passing lines of dialogue and offhand references. But there's plenty to explore in its causes, and Zuckerberg's story ends up feeling bigger than his own life.
reviews.author: Keith Phipps

reviews.text: With spectacular performances, technical elements that are beyond criticism, and the best directorial work of Fincher's remarkable career, The Social Network is one of the best films of 2010.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: This is a remarkable film for more reasons than its antihero... It's a movie as much in the moment as your computer's home page, which for millions of users is Facebook.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Watching The Social Network, the real Zuckerberg may feel as if someone has hacked into his Facebook account and changed his profile picture.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: History as we know it is still unfurling, and The Social Network is that rare film that has something -- not yet definitive, but certainly provocative -- to say about it.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: It's a tribute to Fincher and Sorkin that The Social Network ends up being more absorbing and nuanced than anyone could have hoped.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: The Social Network sees Fincher more ambitious in his narrative choices than ever before, his visual and thematic ideas seemingly multiplying uncontrollably within each frame.
reviews.author: Chris Cabin

reviews.text: The closest to a John Hughes film this generation will get, which is a huge compliment. But, 'The Social Network' is not the defining movie of a generation.
reviews.author: Clay Cane

reviews.text: Has a rhythm, or a pulse. ... You almost interact with the production as you would a stage play, as if the players can feed off your energy (and vice versa).
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: It's not an easy time with this pompous crowd, but the feature encourages the venom to a mesmerizing level of engagement, turning legal woes and verbal abuse into a spellbinding sit.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Possibly the film of the year. Much more than just a facebook movie.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: A smart, literate, engrossing parable of genius, ambition, greed, treachery and inconclusive justice that says a good deal about a world undergoing technological revolution but still beset by the same old human problems.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It's the classic American tale of success, power and greed, but one that's updated for the online generation -- like There Will Be Blood on apps.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Jesse Eisenberg is still recognizable as the kid who starred in "The Squid and the Whale" but Fincher's gotten a new level from the actor...
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: In its quiet way it's every bit as fascinating as Fincher's more self-consciously meaningful films.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: It may be the year's best movie.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The movie zips along at a quick pace, with caffeinated dialogue. Still, things get dull in the third act during the inevitable crash.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Brilliantly directed by David Fincher, this provocative film probes the impetus for invention, the changing face of social interaction and the limits of friendship -- the old-fashioned kind and the version linking 500 million Facebook users.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: David Fincher's film has the rare quality of being not only as smart as its brilliant hero, but in the same way. It is cocksure, impatient, cold, exciting and instinctively perceptive.
reviews.author: Roger Ebert

reviews.text: Cavalier when not in your face cocky, this Hollywood notion of a dumbed down, sexed up Harvard is less brainiac boot camp than Ivy League Club Med where nobody does homework. A hyper-capitalist homage to Facebook, and an infomercial in biopic clothing.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: Despite the ceaseless yammering, The Social Network delivers the heady, rib-tickling rush of an action picture, and it gradually builds to an emotional wallop that blindsides you.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: Like one of those fake-smart, middlebrow TV shows, the speciousness of The Social Network is disguised by topicality. It's really a movie excusing Hollywood ruthlessness.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The film swaggers with a bravado born of insecurity...
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: Smartly written by Aaron Sorkin, directed to within an inch of its life by David Fincher and anchored by a perfectly pitched performance by Jesse Eisenberg, The Social Network is a barn-burner of a tale that unfolds at a splendid clip.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: The Social Network has everything you want in a thriller for the brain: huge doses of ego and duplicity, corporate backstabbing, and some very layered performances.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: So good it can make thrilling even the sight of people typing at computer keyboards.
reviews.author: Matt Soergel

reviews.text: With The Social Network, director David Fincher has come up with a movie that, in telling the turbulent story of whiz-kid Mark Zuckerberg's creation of Facebook, isn't just compelling. It's great.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: On the level of craft, the movie's just absurdly enjoyable.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: A fascinating story about the founding of Facebook and a classic fable about ambition, betrayal, greed, fame, envy, status and sex, the film is an absolute must-see for anyone, on Facebook or not.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: I had more fun watching "The Social Network" than I do snooping Facebook. Post a comment, tag your friends, like this post but get out and see this film!
reviews.author: Jolene Mendez

reviews.text: An altogether mesmerizing tale, filled with unexpected dark humor, that plucks a lot of resonant strings about the Digital Age.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The Social Network combines a multitude of impressions and conflicting first-person accounts in a trajectory that is refreshingly coherent.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: An unforgettable, conversation-provoking, ballsy film.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Because it tackles a big topic and has been made by an important director, critics have been working overtime to position it as some sort of defining film. It's not.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Through deft shooting and a brilliant orchestration of flashforwards and flashbacks, [Fincher and Sorkin] turn these potentially deadly scenes of legal sparring into a zesty narrative framework.
reviews.author: Peter Keough

reviews.text: Addictively entertaining ... tremendously captures a detached-yet-connected Internet age in which people often remain friends online long after the real relationship has dissolved.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: The Social Network succeeds, per journalism's most basic directive, in showing not telling. And like great journalism, a great film can capture the reality of the present -- and even make art out of it.
reviews.author: Eric Hynes

reviews.text: The Social Network's first act is its best -- a hellishly precise youth movie rattling along on a clamor of computer jargon.
reviews.author: J. Hoberman

reviews.text: It zips along, told mostly in flashback, and communicates the pure exhilaration of this momentous social gear-change with aplomb.
reviews.author: Andrew Pulver

reviews.text: A riveting cinematic triumph that can be fairly described as the Citizen Kane of the 21st Century.
reviews.author: Scott A. Mantz

reviews.text: We're talking the internet here, so The Social Network, an analysis of events that took place all of seven years ago, is an ancient history lesson. But it's an illuminating, thoroughly engrossing one. Thrilling, too.
reviews.author: Marc Lee

reviews.text: An unlikely marriage of directorial and writerly sensibilities has produced one of the most stimulating films of the year.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: David Fincher, Aaron Sorkin and a terrific ensemble of young actors reveal the (not quite) true story behind the Facebook phenomenon.
reviews.author: Ethan Alter

reviews.text: Given the remarkably literate, incisive and witty script by Aaron Sorkin, I can think of a half-dozen directors who could have hit this one out of the park.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: The real surprise is that it's also great fun, beginning with a screenplay that represents [Aaron] Sorkin at his very best -- zippy, brainy, amusing, incisive.
reviews.author: Geoff Berkshire

reviews.text: A sharply written tale expressing the irony that a man with five hundred million subscribers has nary a friend in the world.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: An astonishing morality tale about the shadow side of creativity, the loneliness of pioneers, and the ways in which anger can fuel ambition and power in a world ruled by technology.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Just as you can't stop yourself from checking into Facebook more than once a day, you'll find yourself drawn to The Social Network again and again. It's easily one of the year's best.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It is a tremendous entertainment for adults.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Is The Social Network one of the fall season's best big movies? Without question.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: A film this rich emits all kinds of literary and cinematic reverberations.
reviews.author: Richard Corliss

reviews.text: Fincher and his screenwriter, TV writer-god Aaron Sorkin, have made a seemingly modest picture that achieves something close to greatness the old-fashioned, slow-burning way: By telling a story with faces, dialogue and body language of all types.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Among this film's remarkable achievements is that fact that it is thrilling without a single gunshot, in your face without the benefit of 3-D.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A portrait of the generational hero no one asked for, the world he changed by accident, and all the things his invention will never change no matter how hard we try.
reviews.author: Katey Rich

reviews.text: The Social Network is the movie of the year. But Fincher and Sorkin triumph by taking it further. Lacing their scathing wit with an aching sadness, they define the dark irony of the past decade.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: What you're left with is a host of issues far more stimulating than the movie raising them is.
reviews.author: Aaron Cutler

reviews.text: Do movies ever attempt to analyze the entire weave of life? Now they do.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Rushes through a coruscating series of exhilarations and desolations, triumphs and betrayals, and ends with what feels like darkness closing in on an isolated soul.
reviews.author: David Denby

reviews.text: Fincher segments and layers his material at a pace befitting the meteoric ascendancy of Facebook itself, and without the grandstanding that's sometimes marked his work.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: (VIDEO) Jesse Eisenberg does a better job than expected of fulfilling Zuckerberg's identity with an acid-tongued, fast-twitch cyberpunk attitude that wilts every lesser intellect around him.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Poignant, timely, and supremely mounted, Social Network captures the zeitgeist like no other film this year.
reviews.author: Emanuel Levy

reviews.text: Mr. Fincher and Mr. Sorkin offer up a creation story for the digital age and something of a morality tale, one driven by desire, marked by triumph, tainted by betrayal and inspired by the new gospel: the geek shall inherit the earth.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Fincher makes his saga both mesmerizing and fun. Although he moves forward with a constant, pulsing momentum and never stops, in doing so he accurately represents the thrill of sudden inspiration.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: This fascinating, astute 'Rashomon'-like tale is tantalizing, provocative and enthralling, never quite delineating the truth.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A brilliantly layered film ... another home run for Fincher and about as close to perfection one can hope for with such a complex tale.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: an almost-great film whose cultural significance unfortunately outweighs its emotional substance.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: It's the finest film in many years to open the New York Film Festival.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: With a lot of help from Sorkin's (potentially Oscar-worthy) script, David Fincher has crafted his most humorous film since Fight Club.
reviews.author: Erik Davis

reviews.text: On a first viewing, it seems almost indecently smart, funny and sexy. The second time around... half the time I sat there marveling at the similarities of the story, themes and structure to Citizen Kane.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: The Social Network is the movie of the year. If Coppola were into computers, this would be The Godfather.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: A mesmerizing, bewildering and infuriating protagonist makes this movie about Facebook's creation a must-see.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: Continues Fincher's fascinating transition from genre filmmaker extraordinaire to indelible chronicler of our times.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: As socially significant to this generation as films like Network, All The President's Men and The Graduate were in their own time.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

synopsis: In 2003, Harvard undergrad and computer genius Mark Zuckerberg (Jesse Eisenberg) begins work on a new concept that eventually turns into the global social network known as Facebook. Six years later, he is one of the youngest billionaires ever, but Zuckerberg finds that his unprecedented success leads to both personal and legal complications when he ends up on the receiving end of two lawsuits, one involving his former friend (Andrew Garfield). Based on the book "The Accidental Billionaires."
